summary.headline: Wipro Q2 FY27 IT services revenue flat QoQ at $2.61B; Q3 guided -1.5% to +0.5% CC sequential amid furloughs.
summary.overview: IT services revenue was $2.61B, flat sequentially and up 0.6% YoY in constant currency, with operating margin at 16.5%, up 0.5% QoQ on operational improvements and rupee depreciation. TCV fell to $2.6B with nine large deals; management said two large deals slipped on paperwork and are expected to be signed in Q3. Net income declined 5% QoQ to INR32 billion as other income fell 68% after the June 2026 buyback completed, while EPS rose 0.9% QoQ to INR3.23. Q3 guidance is seasonally weak with furloughs and fewer working days.

financial_highlights.change: flat QoQ; +0.6% YoY in constant currency
down QoQ per analyst question; no YoY figure given
-68% QoQ due to lower investable surplus after June 2026 buyback

segments.name: Americas 1
segments.commentary: Declined 2.1% QoQ and 2.7% YoY in constant currency on client-specific issues and healthcare softness.

segments.name: Americas 2
segments.commentary: Grew 0.9% QoQ, declined 4.7% YoY in constant currency; EMR drove sequential growth with BFSI momentum.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 0.6% QoQ and 5.1% YoY in constant currency, led by BFSI, Consumer and EMR.

segments.name: APMEA
segments.commentary: Grew 3.1% QoQ and 13% YoY in constant currency, driven by Consumer, Tech and Comms.

segments.name: BFSI sector
segments.commentary: Grew 1% QoQ and 1.3% YoY in constant currency; a delayed mega-deal ramp is starting and a Europe client's captive insourcing is reversing.

segments.name: Consumer sector
segments.commentary: Grew 2.6% QoQ and 6% YoY in constant currency, helped by new wins and Olam-related revenue.

segments.name: Energy, Manufacturing & Resources (EMR)
segments.commentary: Grew 1% QoQ but declined 6% YoY in constant currency; management cites energy and CPS/engineering wins now ramping.

segments.name: Technology & Communications
segments.commentary: Declined 2.6% QoQ but grew 7% YoY in constant currency.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Declined 3.8% QoQ and 6.5% YoY in constant currency on US payer policy changes; seasonal Q3 benefit expected but smaller than prior years.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 IT services revenue guided to $2.571B to $2.625B, i.e. -1.5% to +0.5% sequential in constant currency.
Q3 impacted by seasonal furloughs; furlough impact expected broadly in line with last year and built into guidance.
Management expects Q4 revenue to benefit from closing the two slipped large deals; no full-year guidance, only quarterly.
Margin: management aims to keep improving margins but gave no timeline to return to the 17-17.5% target band; continued investment in AI Native Unit.
Salary hike effective 1 March 2026 has been rolled out; no further salary increase under consideration.
capex_capacity: AI Native Unit launched April 2026 with over 2,000 engineers, including forward deployed engineers, to drive outcome-based deals.
Five AI growth themes receiving accelerated investment: AI data centers, AI foundry services, physical AI, AI devices and design-to-manufacturing.
Headcount flat YoY; no campus hiring in H1, with campus hiring planned for H2 given volume growth; AI projects driving productivity.
Recent acquisitions HARMAN DTS (engineering, design-to-manufacture) and Mindsprint (food and agri, via Olam deal) cited as contributing capabilities.
demand_pricing: Demand environment described as largely unchanged; clients focused on efficiency while accelerating AI adoption.
Cost optimisation and vendor consolidation remain key drivers; BFSI and Tech named as likely growth leaders.
Deflation: management says contracts average 2 to 2.5 years and the renewal cycle of the last 1.5 to 2 years suggests an inflection in a few quarters.
Nine large deals closed in Q2 with a consulting-led AI transformation win at a global financial institution; mid-market consumer products win for an AI capability centre in India.
Health: first-time outsourcers emerging on cost pressure; US payer policy changes weighed on demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 TCV fall QoQ, and were numbers as expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two deals could not be signed on time in Q2 due to paperwork and will be signed in Q3; Q3 pipeline described as very robust.

qa_highlights.question: Will Wipro use its cash balance for large acquisitions as in the cloud wave?
qa_highlights.answer: Inorganic strategy is consulting-led and AI-powered in priority sectors; acquisitions will continue to be opportunistic, citing HARMAN DTS and Mindsprint as examples.

qa_highlights.question: Is Wipro not benefiting from BFSI recovery seen at peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a delayed mega-deal ramp now starting, a European BFSI client reversing captive insourcing, and Capco growth; BFSI and Tech named as likely growth leaders.

qa_highlights.question: Is the client-specific issue behind us and how much did the Alpha Net tuck-in and Mindsprint contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said client issues are largely behind, with most resolved in Q3. Mindsprint contributed one month of revenue via Olam deal; Alpha Net impact was not material and not quantified. Organic growth figure not separately disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to the 17-17.5% band by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the goal is to improve margins quickly, with operational improvements offsetting investments in AI Native Unit, but no timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 be a positive growth quarter and what drove the Q2 headcount reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 visibility improves if deals close early in Q3. Headcount was flattish YoY; the QoQ reduction reflects no H1 campus hiring, with H2 campus hiring planned.

risks_watch: Conversion of the two slipped large deals in Q3; failure would weaken Q4 revenue visibility.
Health vertical decline (-6.5% YoY) amid US payer policy changes; Q3 seasonal benefit expected to be smaller than prior years.
Americas 1 continued decline and Americas 2 down 4.7% YoY; regional recovery not yet broad.
Margin recovery toward the 17-17.5% band has no timeline and is subject to AI investment spend.
Other income decline (-68% QoQ) will continue to weigh on reported net income after buyback.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management stressed a robust pipeline and confidence in Q3 deal closures, while acknowledging flat revenue, a weak health vertical and no timeline for margin recovery. Answers on BFSI and margin trajectory were somewhat hedged, with the CEO noting that BFSI and Tech could compete for growth leadership.
key_quotes: As far as we are concerned, the pipeline is very robust.
We will continue to make these investments even when they create near-term margin headwinds.
So it is good news that they're getting signed now.
We're not putting a timeline out there.

adds.what: AI Native Unit with over 2,000 engineers (people capacity, not plants; launched April 2026)

growth.why: Q3 FY27 IT services revenue guided to -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ in constant currency ($2.571B to $2.625B), a seasonally weak quarter, with no full-year guidance; growth relies on two slipped large deals expected to sign in Q3 and ramp in Q4, and demand is described as largely unchanged.
